args.fix: Lock the two account rows in a consistent global order (sorted by id) instead of sender-then-receiver, so opposite-direction transfers queue on the same row lock instead of deadlocking. Behaviour otherwise identical.
args.root_cause: transfer() did SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on sender then receiver. Concurrent opposite-direction transfers (A->B and B->A) each hold one row lock and wait for the other, forming a lock-wait cycle that Postgres aborts with 'deadlock detected', failing payments.

text: Fix accepted. Deadlock eliminated by locking rows in sorted-id order.
